keySource: The key is NYSED's own, read from the Map to the Standards in the released-items PDF and carried into provenance/itemmap_g8-2025.json by tools/extract_item_map.py. tools/merge_content.py re-checks every letter against that file item by item and refuses to build if one disagrees, so the key here cannot drift from the official table or be shifted by one released item. Every constructed-response answer below cites NYSED's own exemplary-response page and is checked against this project's transcription of the same item.

G8-2025/q02.png.alt: Four scatter plots labelled A to D, this item's answer choices, each with a straight line drawn through the same set of points.
G8-2025/q02.png.long: Four scatter plots are shown, each plotting the same eight data points on axes marked in single units, x from 0 to 10 and y from 0 to 8, and each with one straight line drawn across it. Plot A is at the upper left, plot C at the upper right, plot B at the lower left, and plot D at the lower right. The eight points, identical in all four plots, are at about (2, 6), (2.6, 6), (3, 4.1), (6.1, 3.2), (6.1, 2.3), (7.9, 2.1), (8.2, 1.9) and (9.8, 1.8); they fall from upper left to lower right. The line in plot A falls from left to right through about (2, 6.3) and (10, 1.8), so it runs above the points through the middle of the plot: where x is 6 the line is at about 4.1 while the two points there are at 3.2 and 2.3. The line in plot C falls a little more steeply, through about (2, 6) and (10, 0.6), so it runs through the middle of the points: where x is 6 the line is at about 3.3, between the points at 3.2 and 2.3, and where x is 8 it is at about 2.0, between the points at 2.1 and 1.9. The line in plot B is horizontal at about y equals 2.9. The line in plot D rises from left to right through about (2, 2) and (10, 7.7), the opposite direction from the points.
